the question of how neuroscience and education can be brought together in a fruitful manner.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the boundary work of bridging the gap is not only a task for the neuroscientists but for all actors involved.
the boundary between science and practice is not bridged, but that it is being worked on.
the boundary between neuroscience and education is not bridged but rather that it is being worked on.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bridging the gap is not a matter of bridging, but of building bridges.
the gap is not only a matter of communication but also of conflicting interests, and that bridging the gap requires a more balanced relationship between neuroscience and education.
bridging the gap requires a change of mindset in both science and practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bridging of science and practice is a social process, in which boundary spanners, boundary objects, boundary work, and boundary objects are important.

the boundary between neuroscience and education is not fixed but can be changed by boundary spanning actors, who can be found in both science and education, and who are willing to work together in order to create new knowledge and practices.

boundary work is not only the responsibility of the neuroscientists and educational professionals, but that it is also the responsibility of policymakers, funding agencies, and other stakeholders to create the conditions for a productive and fruitful collaboration between science and practice.
